name: Shepard-tone endless riser from three mono pitch-bent voices (plus rising noise-filter variant)
goal: Build an endless-rising Shepard-tone riser from any synth: three monophonic copies of one sustained note swept by a full-length pitch-bend ramp, transposed by the sweep span so their ends dovetail, with the top voice fading out and the bottom voice fading in, then grouped into reverb to hide the reset click; plus a variant that applies the same overlap-and-crossfade trick to a ramp-LFO sweep of a resonant comb/flanging filter on white noise for a constantly rising jet/phaser texture.

source.title: Shepard Tone Tutorial - How to Create INFINITE Risers!

prerequisites: Synth with adjustable pitch-bend range and mono (1-voice) mode
Per-voice volume automation and a group/bus with reverb

inputs.name: root_note
inputs.description: Sustained note for the sweep, e.g. middle C

inputs.name: sweep_span_octaves
inputs.description: Total bend span; must be a whole number of octaves (e.g. 2 for +-12 st)

inputs.name: loop_length
inputs.description: Clip length the ramp covers (longer = slower rise)

outputs.name: shepard_riser
outputs.description: Seamlessly looping, apparently endless rising tone/texture

steps.action: Understand the illusion: several copies of the same rising line spaced apart in pitch play together; the lowest copy fades in while the highest fades out, so the ear hears a constant rise.
steps.expect: Plan of 3 voices: high, mid, low

steps.action: Pick any synth where you can set the pitch-bend range and set it to a whole number of octaves (e.g. 12 semitones down and 12 up = a 2-octave sweep).
steps.expect: Full bend covers exactly the planned span

steps.action: Draw one long sustained note across the whole clip and automate pitch bend from its minimum to its maximum exactly over the clip length, so it loops straight from bottom back to bottom.
steps.expect: Single voice sweeps smoothly up and restarts at the loop

steps.action: Duplicate to three voices (high, mid, low). Transpose the high voice up by the sweep span (+2 octaves here) and the low voice down by the same span, so each voice's end pitch equals the next voice's start pitch.
steps.expect: End of the low voice matches start of the mid voice, and so on

steps.action: Set every voice to monophonic (1 voice) so any release tail does not overlap and audibly fade out when the loop restarts.
steps.expect: No ghost tail at the loop point

steps.action: Add volume automation: high voice 100% -> 0% across the clip, low voice 0% -> 100%, mid voice constant. Program the start/end points exactly at the clip boundaries.
steps.expect: Sounds like a constant rise rather than three separate sweeps

steps.action: Group the voices and put reverb on the group: it sits the riser back as a background effect and smooths the small click at pitch reset.
Noise/filter variant: white noise -> a resonant flanging/comb-style filter with many notches; replace the pitch ramp with a rising ramp LFO (retriggered, one ramp per 4 bars) on cutoff.

Make it endless: use four copies; give each a volume fade-in over the first 25% and fade-out over the last 25% of the clip, then duplicate the copies so they overlap and enter in turn (stagger is approximate from transcript).
steps.expect: Constantly rising jet/phaser texture with no audible restarts

verification: Adjacent voices meet at the same pitch at the loop boundary
Muting the fades makes three discrete sweeps audible; with fades it reads as continuous rise
No release-tail artifact at the loop point when voices are mono
Noise variant loops with no audible start/stop of any copy
constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there. Numbers quoted are the presenter's approximate values, in the source tool's own units.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only - map brand UI (Serum/Bitwig/Ableton/Logic/Cubase/Zebra/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for a Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid (Polyrhythm Studio); never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth/DAW vendors named in the source video.
Web Audio mapping: per-voice OscillatorNode.detune ramp (linear in cents = exponential in Hz) plus GainNode fades; reschedule each loop.
Distinct from pitch-ramp risers that simply rise and stop: this is the looping octave-crossfade illusion.
